The core issue is straightforward: the spec requires that all server actions use a non-service-role Supabase client, but `forceLogoutAll` uses the admin client and gets exposed through an API route that only checks for an auth session rather than admin privileges. Any authenticated Discord user can hit that endpoint directly and trigger a global logout. This is a confirmed vulnerability.

There's also a second IDOR issue in the `completeRegistration` function. It accepts a user-supplied QR token, looks up the corresponding temporary registration record using the admin client, and verifies the user exists as a member—but it never checks whether that temporary registration actually belongs to the requesting user. So any authenticated user can claim any unexpired QR token and link any NFC card to their own account. Both findings are legitimate critical-severity issues.
